title: OIDC Device Authorization Grant (RFC 8628)
subtitle: How a smart TV or CLI signs you in: it polls the token endpoint on a back channel while you approve on your phone. The device calls are invisible in a browser; the approval is not.

steps.label: Start sign-in on the device
steps.lede: The user starts sign-in on a constrained device (smart TV or CLI) that has no browser and no easy keyboard. The device will drive the flow over a back channel.
steps.devtools: The device’s calls are not in any browser — inspect them with a proxy (mitmproxy / Charles) or the device/CLI’s own logs. Only the approval on your phone is a normal browser flow you can watch in DevTools.

steps.label: Device authorization request
steps.lede: The device posts its client_id and scope to the device-authorization endpoint. The IdP returns a high-entropy device_code (stays on the device↔IdP channel) and a short human-readable user_code.
steps.devtools: Back-channel (the engine flags it). Read interval (minimum seconds between polls) and expires_in (how long the codes live). device_code is high-entropy and never shown to the human; user_code is the short code they type.

steps.label: Display the code and URL
steps.lede: The device shows the user_code and verification_uri on screen — often with a QR of verification_uri_complete so a phone scan skips manual entry.
steps.code:
To sign in, visit:  https://idp.example.com/activate
and enter code:     WDJB-MJHT

(or scan the QR — it opens
 https://idp.example.com/activate?user_code=WDJB-MJHT )
steps.devtools: Not a network event. The QR encodes verification_uri_complete, which carries the user_code in its query string so the user does not have to type it.

steps.label: Open the verification page
steps.lede: On a second device, the user opens the verification_uri. If they scanned the QR, the user_code arrives in the query string; if they typed it, it arrives in the following form POST.
steps.devtools: This is the part you can watch. In the phone’s DevTools → Network, filter activate. In Query String Parameters you’ll see user_code when the QR was used; if typed, it’s in the subsequent POST body instead. The IdP sets its idp_session cookie here.

steps.label: Authenticate and approve
steps.lede: The user logs in at the IdP and approves the device — the consent screen shows the client name and requested scopes. The IdP then marks the device_code as authorized.
steps.devtools: Confirm the consent screen names the real client and the scopes before approving. The response is typically a “you can return to your device” page. Approving here is what flips the device’s next poll from pending to success.

steps.label: Poll /token — still pending
steps.lede: Meanwhile the device polls the token endpoint every interval seconds with grant_type=device_code. Until the user approves, the IdP answers 400 authorization_pending.
steps.devtools: Back-channel polling. The device must honor interval; if it polls too fast the IdP returns slow_down and the device adds 5s (RFC 8628 §3.5). Other terminal errors: expired_token (codes timed out) and access_denied (user declined).

steps.label: Poll /token — tokens issued
steps.lede: Once the user has approved on the phone, the next poll succeeds: the IdP returns an access token, an ID token, and a refresh token.

jwt.title: Decoded id_token
payload: Stable opaque user id (the account approved on the phone)
Audience — must equal the device client_id
When the user authenticated on the secondary device

steps.devtools: There is no nonce here — the device flow has no front-channel /authorize to carry one; binding is via the device_code on the back channel. Validate the signature (JWKS via kid), then iss, aud == client_id, and exp.

steps.label: Signed in
steps.lede: The device establishes its session from the validated tokens and shows the authenticated UI. It can later use the refresh_token to renew silently.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire. The whole exchange bound a browser login on one device to a session on another, without the constrained device ever handling the user’s password.
